en: Itivuttaka 106: Catukkanipāta, Brāhmaṇadhammayāgavagga Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus! “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Blessed One said this: “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of gifts. What four? The gift of material things, the gift of Dhamma, the gift of safety, and the gift of the Dhamma. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of gifts. When this was said, a certain brahmin approached the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, he said to the Blessed One: “Master Gotama, what is the difference between one who gives a gift of material things and one who gives a gift of Dhamma? “Brahmin, the one who gives a gift of material things gives for the sake of some future worldly fruit; the one who gives a gift of Dhamma gives for the sake of the unsurpassed security from bondage. This, brahmin, is the difference between one who gives a gift of material things and one who gives a gift of Dhamma. When this was said, that brahmin said to the Blessed One: “Magnificent, Master Gotama! Magnificent, Master Gotama! Just as one might set upright what was overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms, even so has Master Gotama explained the Dhamma in various ways. I go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May Master Gotama accept me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life shall last. “Brahmin, one who gives a gift of material things gives for the sake of some future worldly fruit; the one who gives a gift of Dhamma gives for the sake of the unsurpassed security from bondage. The Sabrahmakasutta:
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, those families are 'together with Brahmā' in whose households mother and father are honored by their children."
“Bhikkhus, those families in whose homes the mother and father of their sons are honored are families that have the ancient deities present.
Bhikkhus, those families in whose homes the mother and father of their sons are honored are families that have the ancient teachers present.
Bhikkhus, those families in whose homes the mother and father of their sons are honored are families that have the worthy ones (arahants) present.”
“‘Brahmā,’ monks, is a designation for mother and father.
‘First deity,’ monks, is a designation for mother and father.
‘First teacher,’ monks, is a designation for mother and father.”
“‘Worthy of offerings,’ monks, is a designation for mother and father. And why is that?
Because, monks, mother and father are of great service to their children; they are their nurturers, their sustainers, and those who show them this world.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
"Parents are Brahmā."
They are called the ancient teachers;
they are worthy of offerings from their sons and are compassionate toward their offspring.
Therefore, a wise person should indeed honor and revere them with food and drink.
With clothing and with bedding;
with anointing and bathing,
and with the washing of the feet.
By that service rendered to mother and father, the wise are praised for it even in this very world.
"Having passed away, he rejoices in heaven.
This meaning too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The seventh [sutta].
